steps: Sit facing each other or side by side, with the yarn between you.
Ask if they would prefer to hold the yarn or wind it.
Find the loose end of the yarn together.
Wrap the end around two fingers a few times to start the ball.
Slide it off your fingers and keep winding around that small bundle.
Turn the ball a little every few wraps so it stays round.
Swap jobs whenever either of you would like to.
Tuck the end under the last wrap and drop the ball in the bowl.
safety: Loose yarn is a trip and tangle hazard. Keep it in a basket and gather it up before anyone stands or walks.
Never wrap yarn around a wrist, finger or neck tightly enough to press, and keep long strands away from the neck.
Choose soft yarn that does not shed fibers; some wool can itch or irritate sensitive skin.
Put the yarn away when the activity ends so nobody catches a foot in it later.
cards.stopNote: It is fine to stop with a small ball and plenty of yarn left. Put it all in the basket together and pick it up again another day, or not at all.

cards.name: Wrap a small gift
cards.summary: Wrap a small, unbreakable gift together for someone they choose, then tie it up and add a tag.
materials: A small, unbreakable gift, such as a book or a soft scarf
Wrapping paper, or plain paper or a clean cloth
Ribbon or string, cut in short lengths
Tape
Scissors, kept by the helper
A gift tag or a small piece of card, and a thick pen
steps: Ask who the gift is for and place it on the table in front of them.
Lay out the paper and ask whether they would like to choose a plain or a patterned sheet.
Set the gift in the middle of the paper and fold one side over it.
Bring the other side across and hold it while the helper puts on a piece of tape.
Fold in the two ends and tape them down, one at a time.
Lay the ribbon around the parcel and tie it, or let the helper tie it while they hold the ribbon.
Write the tag together, or let them mark it with a name or a drawing, and tie it on.
Put the finished gift somewhere safe and agree together when to give it.
safety: Keep the scissors with the helper. Cut the paper, tape and ribbon before you start.
Tape can be hard to peel for some hands and can tug on skin. Stick strips to the edge of the table ready to pick up.
Choose a gift that cannot break and has nothing loose that could come off. A book, a scarf or a pack of cards works well.
Use ribbon in short lengths and take it away at the end. Do not leave loose lengths within reach.
cards.stopNote: It is fine to stop at any point. Leave the gift half wrapped, or put it in a bag as it is. The thought of giving is the main part.

cards.name: Write a letter together
cards.summary: Write a short letter or postcard together, with the helper writing as the person says what to put.
materials: A sheet of notepaper or a plain postcard
A pen or pencil that is easy to grip
An envelope and stamp, if the letter will be posted
Optional: a pressed flower and a little tape, or a pencil for a small drawing
steps: Sit side by side at a table with the paper, the pen and the envelope in reach.
Ask who the letter is for and what they would like to say. Any answer is the right one.
Write the greeting at the top, in the words the person chooses.
Ask one open question, such as what has been on their mind this week, and write down the answer.
Read the sentences back aloud and ask if they want to change anything.
Add a drawing, or tape a pressed flower to a corner.
Sign the letter together, then fold it.
Put the letter in the envelope, write the address and add a stamp, or set it aside to give in person.
safety: Never write bank details, passwords or PINs in a letter. Check the address before sealing the envelope.
Keep pens and stamps away from the mouth if the person may chew or taste things.
Check before adding a flower; some plants can cause skin irritation or allergy.
cards.stopNote: It is fine to stop after one sentence. Put the letter aside, and finish it another day, or simply talk about the person it is for.
